    Dashboard Layout Studio Help

    Overview

    Dashboard Layout Studio is a visual layout editor for existing Hubitat Dashboard v1 layouts. It can rearrange, resize, duplicate, remove, and reassign existing tiles, and it can change supported presentation details through custom CSS. It does not replace the Hubitat dashboard and tile configuration interface.

    Use the Hubitat interface for source creation: Create dashboards, create original tiles, choose templates, and configure template-specific properties in the native Hubitat dashboard editor. Reload the dashboard in Dashboard Layout Studio afterward to continue arranging it.
    Dashboard and tile creation limits
    • Dashboard Layout Studio cannot create a new dashboard. The dashboard must first be created in Hubitat.
    • It cannot add a completely new original tile from Hubitat's template list. Additional tiles can be created only by copying or duplicating an existing tile and then changing its supported assignment or layout settings.
    • It cannot change an existing tile from one Hubitat template to another.
    Template-property limits
    • The graphical editor does not change template-specific properties such as custom icons, background images, background settings, or other properties that are not exposed through the layout operations or achievable with CSS.
    • CSS can alter how a tile is displayed, but it does not change the tile's underlying Hubitat template or template configuration.
    • Properties that require the native Hubitat dashboard editor must be changed there, then the dashboard should be reloaded in Dashboard Layout Studio.
    Load & Save

    Opening layouts

    Dashboard Layout Studio can work with layouts that were loaded directly from the hub or with layouts opened from a local file or pasted JSON. In the help text, online and offline describe how the active layout was loaded, not whether the browser or computer is connected to the internet.

    Online mode means the layout was loaded directly from the Hubitat hub. It keeps a hub save target and enables hub-only checks such as device names and selected dashboard devices. When DLS itself is hosted from the hub's /local/ file area, the initial Rendered View capture comes directly from the dashboard being loaded. Later refreshes can use the temporary preview dashboard for unsaved working changes.

    Offline mode means the layout was opened from a file or pasted JSON. Offline layouts can be edited, downloaded, or copied to the clipboard, but they do not have a normal hub save target. When the temporary preview dashboard is enabled and ready, an offline working layout can still be uploaded there solely for Rendered View capture.

    Dashboard launch shortcut: For a clean hub-loaded layout, the shortcut beside the dashboard name opens the saved dashboard immediately. When unsaved changes exist, it becomes a down-arrow menu with choices to open a temporary preview of the unsaved working layout or open the dashboard currently saved on the hub. The shortcut is disabled for offline layouts.

    No cloud connection: DLS does not use the Hubitat cloud. Hub load, save, device checks, temporary preview, and Rendered View capture are performed on the local network against the local hub.

    Load & Save

    Connecting to the hub

    Connect To Hub
    Discovers dashboards from the configured Hubitat hub. Layouts loaded this way keep their hub save target, so Save to hub remains available.
    Hub Connection Settings (Gear Icon)
    Shows hub connection settings: hub IP address, dashboard app number, and access token. When the page is hosted from the hub and those fields are blank, Dashboard Layout Studio tries to fill the dashboard app number and token from /hub2/hubData.
    Auto Discover App & Token
    Reads the current hub's /hub2/hubData information and fills the Dashboard app number and access token. Existing values are replaced only after a Dashboard app with both values is found.
    Dashboard list
    After discovery, choose a dashboard to load its layout into the editor. Shift-click the active dashboard in the list to reload that same dashboard directly from the hub after confirmation.
    Opening offline layouts
    Load file

    Loads a JSON file as an offline layout. Changes to layouts loaded offline cannot be saved directly back to the hub.

    Paste dashboard JSON

    Loads pasted JSON as an offline layout. Like file load, this does not create a hub save target.

    Offline layouts can be edited, downloaded, or copied to the clipboard, but they cannot be saved directly to a hub dashboard unless a hub-loaded layout context is already being preserved through the JSON editor. When you connect to the hub from an offline layout, the offline workspace is closed, the grid and undo history are cleared, and unsaved offline changes require confirmation.
    Load & Save

    Saving and preserving hub context

    Saving and preserving hub context
    Save
    Opens save options: Save to hub, Download as file, or Copy to clipboard. Save to hub is available only when the active layout was loaded from the hub. Preferences can skip save-time device checks when you intentionally manage selected dashboard devices yourself.
    Important hub-save distinction

    If you load a layout with the side panel file/paste tools, the tool treats it as offline JSON.

    If you instead load from the hub and then use the JSON editor to replace or edit the layout, the existing hub save target is preserved.

    JSON editor replacement warning: When a hub-loaded layout is replaced from the JSON editor, the editor warns that it is still attached to the online dashboard. Saving afterward will overwrite that same hub dashboard with the replacement layout. Use the side-panel file/paste tools when you want to open JSON as an offline layout instead.
    Selecting Tiles

    How tile selection works

    Selecting individual tiles and stacks

    Like the Hubitat native editor, each tile location is defined by the row and column of the tile’s upper-left corner. Dashboard Layout Studio uses that same upper-left-corner location when deciding whether a tile belongs to a row, column, or rectangular selection.

    A tile may extend beyond the selected area because its height and width span additional grid cells. The Selection mode controls whether a tile whose upper-left corner is outside the target—but whose span crosses into it—is included, excluded, or selected by itself as a partial tile.

    Click a tile
    Selects the tile at that cell. Repeated clicks on the same overlapped cell cycle through the stack.
    Ctrl/Cmd-click tile
    Adds or removes a tile from the current tile selection. On overlapped stacks, repeated Ctrl/Cmd-clicks cycle through layers.
    Alt-click tile
    Selects the connected tile cluster at that cell.
    Double-click tile/grid cell
    Selects the connected tile cluster at that cell.
    Selecting areas, rows, and columns
    Drag on grid
    Creates a rectangular selection. The Selection mode option determines which crossing tiles are included.
    Ctrl/Cmd-drag grid
    Adds the rectangular drag selection to the current tile selection.
    Click row/column header
    Selects that row or column as a line selection.
    Drag row/column headers
    Selects a contiguous row or column range.
    Shift-click header
    Extends the row or column selection from the previous header anchor.
    Right-click grid/header
    Opens a context menu for tile, empty cell, row, or column actions.
    Selection mode
    default

    Selects tiles located in the target area by their upper-left row/column.

    incl partial

    Also includes tiles that start outside the target but cross into it.

    excl partial

    Limits the result to tiles fully contained in the target.

    only partial

    Selects only tiles crossing the target boundary; intended for clear-type cleanup work.

    Toolbar Buttons

    Selection and tile actions

    How the toolbar is organized

    The first toolbar group in the top row contains actions that operate on the current selection: tiles, rows, columns, or selected areas.

    The next top-row group contains whole-layout actions such as Trim and Spacing.

    Select first, then act. Selection actions use the current tile, row, column, or rectangular selection; whole-layout actions operate across the dashboard layout.
    Selection and structural actions
    Select
    Selects all tiles in the layout. This is the toolbar equivalent of Ctrl/Cmd+A.
    Info
    Click to show tile id, position, size, device id from the layout JSON, hub device name when available, template details, and tile-scoped custom CSS for the selected tile. Hold or Shift-click for the Info menu, which also opens Reports. When no tile is selected, Tile Information remains visible in the menu but is disabled. The scoped CSS section can be edited directly; every saved selector must remain scoped to the current tile.
    Reports
    Opens from the Info hold menu. Creates printer-friendly Plain, Relationship Tree, Overlap Groups, Nested Groups, or Conflict Groups reports for either the selected tiles or the whole layout. Reports open in a separate window, support configurable sorting, selectable columns, common paper sizes, and portrait, landscape, or automatic orientation. Grouped reports can optionally include a proportional thumbnail showing each group’s actual tile footprints and overlaps. Reports are paginated into true paper-sized sheets with a header, footer, and page number on every page. Column headings repeat on every table page. Graphical relationship groups remain together when they fit; oversized groups continue across pages with repeated group headings, fixed readable typography, and connected hierarchy cards rather than page-wide text scaling.
    Insert
    For row/column selections, inserts rows or columns before the selected line range and shifts affected tiles. With incl partial, tiles that start before the inserted line but cross into the selected range move with the selected tiles.
    Delete
    Deletes selected rows/columns and shifts later tiles to close the gap. For tile selections, use Clear to remove without shifting.
    Clear
    Removes selected tiles or tiles in the selected area without shifting other tiles.
    Placement and clipboard actions
    Move to
    Starts a placement operation. Click a destination cell or compatible row/column header to move the selection.
    Copy to
    Starts a placement operation that duplicates the selection to a clicked destination.
    Cut / Copy / Paste
    Uses an internal tile buffer. Cut keeps tiles visible until the first paste, which behaves as a move; later pastes create copies.
    Toolbar Buttons

    Layout and editor controls

    Layout sizing and spacing actions
    Trim
    Whole-layout action that removes blank space above and/or left of the current layout. Hold the button for top-only or left-only choices.
    Resize
    Selection-action button that sets selected tiles to an exact height and width. Options can preserve spacing between resized tiles and/or push the surrounding layout out of the way. When Overlaps is set to push, or Shift is held, the Resize button glows and the dialog opens with Preserve spacing between resized tiles and Push layout to make room enabled.
    Spacing
    Opens a dialog with all spacing actions: Set all, Set rows only, Set columns only, Unstack and Set All, Inc/Dec all, Inc/Dec rows only, and Inc/Dec columns only.
    Enl/Rdc
    Opens the Enlarge / Reduce dialog for enlarging or reducing the entire layout by row and column amounts. Positive rows/columns enlarge tiles; negative rows/columns reduce them. This is equivalent to selecting all tiles and dragging the lower-right resize handle.
    Unstack and Set All
    Set-menu option that is enabled only when tiles overlap. It breaks overlap stacks apart and sets spacing between individual tiles.
    Spacing value
    In the Spacing dialog, positive values increase spacing, negative values decrease spacing, and zero disables Inc/Dec while still allowing Set actions.
    History, views, JSON, and Save
    Undo / Redo / Undo All
    Step backward, step forward, or restore the layout to the state it had when first loaded. Undo All follows undo history and remains disabled when there is no undo checkpoint. For hub-loaded layouts, Undo All restores the hub-equivalent state and refreshes Rendered View instead of disabling it. Shift-click Undo All reloads the current dashboard from the hub when the layout originated from the hub and Undo All is enabled; otherwise it performs the normal Undo All action.
    Rendered View engine
    Preferences can choose the Rendered View startup engine: Style Copy clones rendered tile HTML and computed styles, Image Snapshot uses image-style tile snapshots and keeps styled HTML for icon-font tiles when the image converter cannot preserve dashboard icons, Compatibility Mode starts with the mobile-compatible hidden dashboard frame, and Simple View Only disables Rendered View. By default, DLS creates or reuses an internal dashboard named DLS Temporary Dashboard. When a dashboard is first loaded from the hub, DLS captures rendered tiles directly from that loaded dashboard and does not update the temporary dashboard. For later manual refreshes, DLS authorizes the devices used by the current working layout, saves that layout only to the temporary dashboard, and captures rendered tiles there without changing the active dashboard or its save target. The temporary dashboard is hidden from the normal dashboard list and remains on the hub for reuse. If Use temporary preview dashboard is disabled or the temporary dashboard is unavailable, DLS uses the original dashboard-rendering workflow and retains the existing warnings when unsaved tile content, device, CSS, HTML, JS, or other render-affecting changes would not appear in the capture.
    JSON
    Opens the editable JSON editor for direct layout edits, formatting, load-file-into-editor, copy, download, and apply.
    Save
    Choose hub save, file download, or clipboard copy.
    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Move, copy, paste, and overlaps

    Placement operations

    Move to, Copy to, and Paste put the editor into a pending placement mode.

    1. Choose Move to, Copy to, or Paste.
    2. Click the destination grid cell.
    3. Use Escape to cancel the pending operation.
    Push behavior

    Push is available for a single tile or a single connected cluster. It is disabled for disconnected multi-cluster selections or buffers.

    When push is used, tiles to the right and/or below the destination are moved enough to make room.

    Overlap handling and CSS duplication
    Overlaps: warn
    Blocks operations that would overlap existing tiles.
    Overlaps: allow
    Allows the operation even if resulting tiles overlap.
    Overlaps: skip
    Skips conflicting copied/moved tiles when possible.
    Overlaps: push
    Moves affected tiles to make room, using the Push buf value as an added gap.
    Dup CSS
    When copying tiles, duplicates tile-scoped custom CSS for the new tile ids.
    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Spacing and direct manipulation

    Spacing and unstacking

    Spacing Set normally treats touching or overlapping tiles as connected clusters, so spacing is adjusted between clusters without breaking them apart.

    Unstack and Set All is available only when the layout has actual overlapping tiles. It treats every tile as its own unit, moves tiles as needed, and sets the requested spacing while removing overlaps.

    This is the GUI equivalent of using spacing set with overlap removal for all tiles.

    Dragging and resizing
    Move by dragging

    Drag selected tiles directly on the grid to move them. If the dragged tile is already overlapped with another tile, Overlaps is temporarily treated as Allow for that drag so the tile can be moved while remaining overlapped. The previous Overlaps setting is restored when the mouse button is released.

    Resize by dragging

    Drag the resize handle at the bottom-right of a selected tile to resize the selection.

    Mouse-resize behavior

    Mouse resizing grows from the upper-left corner and adjusts neighboring selected tiles to avoid growing over each other.

    Exact size

    The Resize dialog does the same kind of spacing-aware resize, but uses an exact height and width entered by the user.

    The Enl/Rdc (Enlarge / Reduce) dialog applies that same resize-drag behavior to the full layout by treating every tile as selected and applying row/column deltas.

    Grid settings and editor grid view

    The Grid dialog changes the dashboard grid metadata and cell sizes. The current grid summary and editable grid values stay visible at the top of the dialog while the lower area is organized into tabs. The grid change mode is shown in the main Grid Settings box and offers two choices: Change grid only and Preserve layout. Use the question-mark icon next to the Grid change mode title to compare the modes. Change grid only keeps tile coordinates untouched. Preserve layout is experimental and changes tile positions and spans to keep the dashboard as close as possible to its current visual geometry. Because Hubitat tile coordinates and spans are whole numbers, DLS warns when an enlarged grid cannot preserve the current geometry exactly; when Preserve layout is selected, Column Size and Row Size are constrained so no existing tile would have to shrink below 1×1. Preserve layout uses a relationship-first scale pass: connected, nested, and overlapped tiles are scaled with shared rounded grid lines; positive margins and empty-cell gaps remain visible; and container/background tiles grow only as needed so nested or overlay tiles stay inside and aligned. The Recommended tab is enabled only when Preserve layout is selected and scores preservation-friendly Column Size / Row Size / Grid Gap combinations for the current layout. It evaluates columns and rows independently, so dashboards with different column and row sizes still get useful sweet-spot recommendations. The Auto Fit tab calculates Column Size / Row Size / Grid Gap values for a target screen and includes expanded presets for common PCs, Macs, Fire tablets, kiosk/wall displays, tablets, phones, plus a remembered custom size. Fire and kiosk presets use full-screen display dimensions for wall-dashboard use, including Fully Kiosk Browser setups. The Statistics tab compares current and new dashboard size side by side and lists warnings. The CSS Issues tab is enabled only when Preserve layout is selected and issues are detected; issues are grouped by change type, such as font/icon sizes or padding/fixed-size CSS. Each group has one Fix checkbox and lists the matching CSS declarations plus the proposed scaled value, so users can apply font fixes while leaving padding or positioning CSS unchanged. Toolbar buttons use two menu indicators: a full down arrow means the button always opens a menu, while a small corner marker means the button has a normal click action plus hold/Shift-click alternates. The Grid toolbar button uses the full arrow and opens a dropdown with Edit and Trim. Edit opens this Grid Settings dialog; Trim immediately sets the declared Grid Columns/Rows to the current used layout area. The toolbar rows are balanced so the second-row settings group is widened only enough to match the first row after the Grid dropdown was added. The dialog footer includes Reset to Current, which restores the dialog fields to the current dashboard grid values. DLS always preserves dashboard row/column aspect ratio and shows grid gaps by default; Preferences includes a Don't show grid gap option for a tighter editing view and an Auto-size dashboard bounds option that grows or shrinks declared rows/columns to the used layout plus optional padding. The Grid Zoom control in the lower bar provides a slider, an Actual button, and a Fit button. Dashboards load in Fit view by default so the whole used layout is visible. Actual jumps to the dashboard cell size and gap regardless of fit. Fit zooms the used layout into the editor area without shrinking displayed row/column cells below 3px. When zoomed out, DLS keeps drawing enough rows and columns to fill the editor viewport so the blank canvas is not mistaken for a layout boundary. Applying grid-size changes switches the editor to Actual view so the new dashboard cell sizes can be inspected immediately. The displayed grid size appears at the lower right after the legend. Dashboards with Column Size or Row Size set to 0 are treated as dynamic Auto-sized dashboards. DLS simulates only the dynamic axis: Column Size 0 uses the Auto Fit target width, Row Size 0 uses the Auto Fit target height, and any fixed axis keeps its explicit dashboard size. When a dynamic dashboard is loaded, DLS shows a notice explaining which Auto Fit preset is being used and offers a button to open Grid Settings → Auto Fit; the notice can be suppressed. The lower status area shows the active dynamic preset, and the grid size readout labels dynamic and fixed axes separately. DLS draws a yellow dashed Dynamic target boundary on the grid so 0-sized dashboards, including 0 / 0 / 0 layouts, remain readable. When Grid Gap is 0, DLS writes it as quoted "0" in saved/exported JSON to avoid the Hubitat zero-gap reset issue.

    Move, Copy & Spacing

    Resize selected tiles

    Resize dialog: preserving spacing and growing
    Preserve spacing between resized tiles

    Preserves the original spacing between the selected tiles while their sizes change.

    Push layout to make room

    If the target size is larger than the selected tiles, the layout option is Push layout to make room. It automatically enables Preserve spacing between resized tiles and moves affected surrounding tiles to make room, using the same push buffer and overlap behavior as Move to, Copy to, and Paste.

    Resize dialog: reducing, pulling, and conflicts
    • If the target size is smaller than the selected tiles, the option changes to Pull layout to close gaps.
    • When Pull layout to close gaps is unchecked, unselected tiles do not move; only the selected tiles resize, though Preserve spacing between resized tiles can still move selected tiles relative to each other to preserve their internal gaps.
    • When Pull layout to close gaps is checked, every row/column band freed by the shrink is removed from downstream tiles, so the collapse continues through the full layout rather than stopping at the first nearby row or column.
    • When multiple selected tiles form one adjacent cluster with no unselected tiles between them, their internal spacing is preserved regardless of gap size, and the surrounding layout is pushed or pulled using the resized cluster's combined outside footprint.
    • If an unselected tile sits between selected tiles, Resize Push/Pull is blocked instead of treating the selection as separate pieces.
    • Without Push/Pull layout, conflicts are handled by the Overlaps setting: warn, allow, or skip.
    • If the entered size enlarges any selected tile and would create overlaps, the Resize dialog shows a live warning.
    • With Overlaps set to allow, the warning indicates that overlaps will be allowed.
    • With Overlaps set to warn, pressing Resize opens a confirmation so the user can cancel or deliberately proceed creating the overlaps.
    JSON & CSS

    JSON editor and applying changes

    JSON editor and field views
    JSON editor
    Allows direct edits, cut/copy/paste, formatting, downloading, copying, and loading a JSON file into the editor text area. The Copy button copies the visible editor pane as formatted plain text so line breaks and indentation paste correctly into tools such as Notepad.
    custom field views
    The customCSS, customHTML, and customJS buttons switch the editor to only that field. Edits sync back into the full JSON when you switch views, format, copy, download, or apply.
    Tile Devices
    Lists every tile by ID, its grid location and size, any tile-scoped CSS content that may supply an alternate title, and its assigned device. Location and size are shown as row/column followed by size in parentheses. The first device choice is Unassigned for blank device IDs. Online layouts use the same selected-device choices as Tile Information; device dropdowns are sorted by device name with the device number shown in parentheses. Offline layouts allow numeric or blank device IDs. In online mode, tiles with a nonblank, nonzero device ID that has no matching hub device are treated as unknown-device tiles and highlighted in red, except Mode and Text Tile templates because those device fields are not validated as regular hub-device assignments. Tile-device rows for valid hub devices that are not selected for the dashboard are highlighted in yellow and remain unselected until you explicitly add them in Dashboard Devices. A Preferences option can skip this save-time device validation while leaving the editor review tools available. Show Invalid and Unassign Invalid are online-only tools. Unassign Invalid clears every non-exempt tile device assignment whose device ID does not exist on the hub after confirmation.
    Dashboard Devices
    Online only. Manages the devices selected for the Hubitat dashboard, locks devices used by current tiles, and can assign all devices, remove unused devices, reload the selection, or update it on the hub. Devices with assigned tiles that are not currently selected are marked yellow and remain unchecked until explicitly selected. Devices that are selected and assigned to tiles are shown in a slightly faded blue locked state.
    Applying editor changes

    Apply changes validates and replaces the current working layout. JSON editor commits are normal edits and create an Undo checkpoint before the layout is replaced.

    Custom field-only edits

    If only a customCSS, customHTML, or customJS field view is committed, existing Rendered View captures are kept but marked as not reflecting those manual changes until refreshed.

    Full JSON edits

    Full JSON edits still invalidate Rendered View captures.

    If the layout was loaded from the hub, the hub save target is preserved.

    Use the JSON editor when you want to replace the layout while preserving hub context. Use side panel Load file/Paste JSON when you want to open an offline layout.
    JSON & CSS

    CSS validation and cleanup

    Validate / Format

    Validates and formats the currently visible editor view. Full JSON is JSON-formatted; customHTML and customJS use very basic formatting and limited sanity checks. In customCSS view, the button opens choices for Validate / Reg Fmt or Validate / Comp Fmt.

    In customCSS view, the format step opens a review dialog when it finds:

    Duplicates

    Duplicate selector/property declarations.

    Conflicts

    Conflicting declarations for the same selector/property.

    Orphans

    Tile rules that reference tiles no longer present.

    Consolidation

    Repeated selector rules that can be combined.

    Conflicts are grouped with value bubbles and the current cascade winner selected automatically. Each issue row has a consistent skip checkbox, and the Preserve removed CSS footer option can keep removed duplicates, conflicts, and orphans inactive instead of deleting them.

    CSS cleanup processing and options
    • Duplicate declarations are removed before selector consolidation.
    • Consolidation rewrites repeated selector rules into one rule and does not preserve the original repeated rules.
    • Consolidation rows with unresolved related conflicts are labeled Conflicts Found, unchecked, and disabled. Resolve the related conflicts first, then reopen or reanalyze CSS Cleanup before applying that consolidation.
    • Duplicates and consolidation choices are listed with preselected checkboxes so you can accept or skip each cleanup.
    • Applying selected cleanup to the current working layout creates a normal Undo checkpoint.
    • The cleanup dialog applies only the selected fixes unless Reformat after applying fixes is checked.
    • Validate / Comp Fmt first runs the regular CSS formatter and then applies the same compact one-rule-per-line output, split selector lists, condensed rule bodies, and CLI-like sorting as the customCSS tab compact formatter.
    • When any selector consolidation is applied, all preserved duplicate comments are removed because every duplicate is already represented by a surviving active declaration. This includes comments inside selectors that were already in a single rule and comments preserved by an earlier cleanup run.
    CSS status and tile scope
    CSS status indicator
    Appears when customCSS validation finds conflicts, duplicate declarations, orphaned tile rules, or selector consolidations. Green indicates optional cleanup suggestions, yellow indicates non-critical cleanup items such as orphans or duplicates, and red indicates CSS conflicts that should be reviewed. The cleanup dialog can remove selected items or preserve removed duplicate, conflict, and orphan CSS in inactive form; orphan preservation uses one Removed Orphaned Rules and comments block, and orphaned tile-scoped comments are removed or preserved with the related orphan cleanup. CSS cleanup checks use the merged effective stylesheet, including imported @import rules plus editable customCSS, for conflicts, duplicates, and selector consolidation. Imported conflicts, duplicates, and consolidation candidates are separated from editable customCSS items because imported rules are read-only. Consolidated selector originals are not preserved. Consolidation is blocked whenever related conflicts are found, and those rows show Conflicts Found until the conflicts are resolved.
    Device status indicator
    Appears next to CSS Status in online mode when tile device assignments need review. Red indicates one or more non-exempt tile device IDs do not exist on the hub; clicking it opens the JSON Editor to Tile Devices. Yellow indicates valid hub devices are assigned to non-exempt tiles but are not selected for the dashboard; clicking it opens the JSON Editor to Dashboard Devices. Mode and Text Tile templates are excluded from these validity checks.
    Tile-scoped CSS
    Rules such as #tile-40, #tile_40, or .tile-40 are treated as tile-scoped CSS for copy/cleanup operations. If customCSS contains @import stylesheets, DLS loads imported tile-scoped rules as read-only external CSS. Imported rules are displayed in the customCSS editor and Tile Info, included in merged CSS conflict, duplicate, and consolidation checks with editable customCSS, and copied into editable customCSS when matching tiles are duplicated. External conflicts are shown separately with options to discard the editable customCSS declaration or accept the conflict. The External CSS Rules indicator appears when imported tile-scoped rules are active.

    Keyboard shortcuts

    Keyboard shortcuts
    Ctrl/Cmd + Z
    Undo.

    Ctrl/Cmd + Y
    Redo.

    Select all tiles, when not typing in an input/editor.

    Shortcuts

    Mouse combinations

    Mouse combinations
    Click tile
    Select tile; repeated clicks on the same overlapped cell cycle layers.
    Ctrl/Cmd-click tile
    Toggle tile in multi-selection; repeated clicks on overlapped cells cycle/toggle layers.
    Alt-click tile
    Select the connected cluster.
    Double-click tile/cell
    Select the connected cluster.
    Drag selected tile
    Move the selected tile or selected group. Already-overlapped tiles can be dragged while temporarily allowing the existing overlap; the previous Overlaps setting returns after drop.
    Drag resize handle
    Resize selected tiles from their lower-right edge.
    Drag grid background
    Create a rectangular tile selection.
    Ctrl/Cmd-drag grid
    Add a rectangular selection to the existing selection.
    Click/drag header
    Select one row/column or a contiguous row/column range.
    Shift-click header
    Extend row/column selection from the previous header anchor.
    Right-click grid/header
    Open the context menu.
    Shift-click active dashboard
    Reload the currently active dashboard from the hub from the left dashboard list, after confirmation.
    Shift-click Undo All
    For a hub-originated layout, reload the current dashboard from the hub when Undo All is enabled. For other layouts, perform normal Undo All.
    Press and hold toolbar buttons
    Open alternate options on buttons with a dropdown arrow, such as push placement, trim direction, spacing scope, and save destination.

    Save to hub

    You can download a backup of the original loaded layout before overwriting.

    Hub connections unavailable

    This page can only connect to your Hubitat hub when it is hosted by the hub itself. Browsers block cross-origin requests due to CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing) restrictions, which prevent pages loaded from one location from accessing resources on another.

    To enable hub connections:

    1. Open your Hubitat hub's web interface
    2. Go to Settings → File Manager
    3. Upload this HTML file to the hub
    4. Open the file from the hub (e.g. http://<hub-ip>/local/dashboard-layout-studio.html)

    You can still use this tool offline by loading a dashboard JSON file using Load file… or Paste JSON.

    Preserve removed CSS
    
    
    
      
    When checked, duplicate and conflicting declarations are placed in CSS comment blocks instead of being deleted. Duplicate comments are retained only when no selector consolidation is applied. When consolidation runs, all preserved duplicate comments are removed because each duplicate is already represented by a surviving active declaration, including comments inside selectors that were already in one rule and comments preserved by an earlier cleanup run. Orphaned tile rules and orphaned tile-scoped comments are removed together, or moved into one Removed Orphaned Rules and comments. comment block when Preserve removed CSS is checked, with active tile selectors such as #tile-5 or .tile-5 changed to inactive selectors such as #tile_5 or .tile_5. Consolidated selector rules are not preserved; consolidation always replaces repeated selector rules with one combined rule after conflicts and duplicates have been processed.
